loci.name: l2-residual-after-ribeiro-base-instruct-reasoning-format
loci.one_line: After Ribeiro et al. and the shift/robustness citers, is any L2 factor (base vs instruct, post-training stage, reasoning on/off, verbal elicitation format) both unstudied on code with execution labels AND plausibly different from general NLP (A21 test), or does the pivot-1/2 union already close it?
loci.rationale: Contradiction cluster 0/6/5: Ribeiro (on-llms-internal-representation-of-code-correctness) shows probe beats verbal on 4 instruct 7-8B models but only whole-solution, zero-shot verbal, no AUROC/ECE, no base pairs, no reasoning models. The 'which-signals' paper (Qwen3-Coder-30B, gpt-oss-20b) finds the probe advantage setting-dependent (Table II BCB->LCB probe .480 vs confidence .552) and disables reasoning; the robustness paper shows probe accuracy flips with framing (37-55% neutral vs 63-69% concept). Base-vs-instruct on code is touched only by the SAE paper (Gemma-2-2b, MBPP only, no verbal readout), post-training stages only in math (post-training-shifts-confidence, Qwen2.5-7B, token prob, AUROC 0.320 for RL), reasoning-vs-nonreasoning for code only verbal-only (do-large-language-models-know-what-they-are-capable-of). Whether these shards form a union (A20) or leave a concrete residual decides L2 NARROW vs OCCUPIED(union) and whether L2 stays the spine.

opposing_positions.position: L2 is occupied or occupied-by-union: probe-beats-verbal on code, shift robustness, SAE base-to-instruct persistence, and verbal reasoning-vs-nonreasoning together leave only a models/benchmarks change; general-NLP direction (post-training hurts token calibration, reasoning helps verbal) transfers.

A concrete residual survives: no work crosses probe x verbal x sampling with execution labels over base/instruct pairs and reasoning on/off; code-specific reasons (executable ground truth, instruct raises certainty on failing code, probes fragile to framing) make the general-NLP direction non-transferable.

suggested_searches: base versus instruct code LLM calibration token uncertainty execution
reasoning mode on off probe verbalized confidence code correctness
post-training stage SFT RLHF code calibration pass/fail
pivot criterion 1 union check: same-problem probe verbal sampling code

loci.name: probe-advantage-vs-difficulty-and-supervision-artifact
loci.one_line: Is the probe-over-verbal gap on code a real disconnect, or an artifact of problem-difficulty confounding, many-shot supervision vs zero-shot verbal, and prompt-only baselines (decides whether L2's central claim needs within-problem, supervision-matched controls)?
loci.rationale: Clusters 3 and 10. which-signals paper: predictors transfer 'largely by identifying difficult problems', within-problem ranking limited, EigenScore no consistent advantage. disentangling-task-difficulty and hard-issue-weak-model papers (agents) report run-blind difficulty references match predictors. Opposing: a-heckler-in-the-hidden-state and 260614530 (pre-generation probes survive length controls) report within-problem signal. Outside code, cognitive-dissonance, can-llms-introspect-a-reality-check and measurement-validity show probe superiority tied to supervised training and prompt-only TF-IDF baselines matching probes in 9 of 11 cells. Ribeiro uses same-task correct/incorrect pairs (within-task) but a trained probe vs zero-shot verbal, so the fairness of the comparison is unresolved. Directly bears on pivot criterion 2/3 (A14: does trained verbal or recalibration close the gap in discrimination) and on what L2/L1 controls are mandatory for TMLR 'convincing evidence'.

opposing_positions.position: Within-problem signal exists and probes (incl. pre-generation, length-controlled) separate correct from incorrect variants of the same task; probe-beats-verbal reflects real unexpressed information.
Pooled AUROC is dominated by cross-problem difficulty; probe superiority is supervision asymmetry and prompt-only baselines match; the 'disconnect' is partly artifact.

suggested_searches: within-problem AUROC code correctness probe difficulty baseline
supervised verbal confidence vs probe matched supervision
prompt-only baseline matches probe code correctness

loci.name: l3-confidence-routed-execution-vs-random-oracle-and-revision-after-failure
loci.one_line: Does any code study evaluate elicited or probed confidence as an execution-budget router against random AND oracle routing with execution labels, and does verbal confidence update (validly) after a failing test? Decides L3 component verdicts.
loci.rationale: Cluster 7 and 14. Closest occupants are partial: heteroskedastic-signals (MBPP, Random/Thr/CST/Oracle, Table 1: Rand .551, Thr .636, Oracle 1.00) but logit proxy only, injected label noise; swe-verifier (261030284) gates by a trained verifier, no random baseline at matched rate in Table 1; the 1introduction paper finds uncertainty-triggered regeneration hurts Pass@1 in 5 of 6 configs but verification-based helps, n=31; give-up-to-get-more finds cheap priors give no gain over round-robin and swe-router shows little gain. Revision: do-large-language-models-know-what-they-are-capable-of shows per-tool-call restated confidence degrades for Claude and modestly improves for OpenAI (SWE-bench), but without valid-vs-spurious failure contrast; resist-and-update and not-one-belief show confidence drops under mere persistence. A7 (revision tracks repair outcome with correct vs spurious failures) looks CLEAN/NARROW; routing-vs-oracle looks NARROW with a stated residual (verbal/probe signal, execution labels). Resolve which side the evidence supports.

opposing_positions.position: Uncertainty-gated allocation beats random/uniform under budgeted verification in code and agents; some models improve discrimination as tool calls accrue.

Little or no routing gain from cheap priors/uncertainty (regeneration hurts, round-robin matches, discrimination does not predict routing utility); confidence moves with persistence or pressure not with evidence.

suggested_searches: confidence routing oracle random baseline code execution budget
verbal confidence update after failing unit test self-repair outcome
selective verification coding agent random matched verify rate

loci.name: l1-estimator-sensitivity-and-label-oracle-dependence
loci.one_line: Do method rankings in code confidence studies change with the calibration estimator (ECE vs Brier skill vs AUROC/AURC) and with the execution-label oracle (thin vs augmented tests), and has this been shown on code? Decides whether L1's measurement-protocol components are CLEAN/NARROW or OCCUPIED.
loci.rationale: Clusters 13, 8, 11. Authors in the corpus (localized-calibrated-uncertainty 251224560 Sec 3; measurement-validity: low-ECE verbal has ~2.02x lower Murphy resolution than sampling; verbalized-uncertainty-in-coding-llms: lowest ECE 0.013 with AUROC 0.49; tce, when-calibration-rankings-reverse) argue ECE misleads, yet security-calibration, ConfTuner and others headline ECE. Recalibration: Spiess (240202047) and multicalibration report Platt/group gains, but characterizing-overconfident-failure and decomposing-probabilistic-scores find Brier skill near base rate. Label side: EvalPlus, SWE-ABS, certified-against-which-oracle (conformal risk shifts with oracle) vs code-is-more-than-text and functional-entropy using hidden-suite pass as gold. Neither side has a code study with multiple confidence families AND estimators AND augmented-test labels in one design, which is the L1 protocol residual (A1, A8, A10).

opposing_positions.position: ECE and single-oracle labels are invalid or unstable instruments: rankings reverse with estimator/accuracy control, thin test suites and oracle choice change reported risk and favor same-oracle scores.
Standard practice is adequate: hidden-suite pass as gold and ECE/Platt gains are the reported headline evidence and are accepted as sufficient for ranking methods.

suggested_searches: code confidence ranking changes with calibration metric AUROC ECE Brier
augmented test labels calibration code LLM EvalPlus confidence
release-date contamination calibration LiveCodeBench

loci.name: f-metrology-and-metacognitive-efficiency-occupancy
loci.one_line: Do measurement-validity / SDT type-2 / Murphy-Yates works (non-code) already define readout bias, resolution relative to an internal reference, and cross-format noise, so that F fails A24 (no new computable quantity)?
loci.rationale: Cluster 20. measurement-validity-and-representation-dynamics (pre-registered audit of verbal, probe, sampling on Qwen2.5; 3 verbal formats Spearman 0.126/-0.069/0.247; Murphy resolution) names Mahaut 2024 and DECK as closest prior; do-llms-know-what-they-know (meta-d' efficiency), llms-as-signal-detectors (sensitivity/bias), dont-ask-understanding-numeric-self-reports, 260305544 (Yates rearrangement) and 260315232 (decomposing probabilistic scores) overlap the bias/resolution/noise trio. Counter: uncertainty-evaluation-bridging-ML-and-measurement-science and the GUM/VIM classification paper put generative systems out of scope. The corpus gestures at occupancy but no note maps each candidate quantity (readout bias, resolution vs internal reference, cross-format noise) onto its closest existing quantity; F's verdict (OCCUPIED vs NARROW as framing only) hinges on that mapping. Foundations (Murphy, Fleming and Lau) are instrument gaps.
suggested_searches: Mahaut 2024 confidence verbal vs internal probability alignment
DECK Chauhan confidence measurement
meta-d prime LLM probe verbal readout efficiency
readout noise across elicitation formats decomposition Brier

loci.name: l4-localization-occupancy-line-vs-test-group-and-targeted-repair
loci.one_line: Does line/token/step-level localized confidence (251224560, FLARE, faulty-token localization, AdaDec) already occupy per-requirement/test-group confidence, and is targeted repair guided by confidence vs regeneration tested under matched budget?
loci.rationale: Cluster 18, 4. 251224560 gives probe-calibrated line-level edit probabilities (BSS ~0.2 vs negative for token prob and verbal line ratings) on four benchmarks, labeled by minimal-repair edits, marking localization OCCUPIED at line level but with no test-group unit. Repair side: self-debug, FLARE, hierarchical debugging win; is-self-repair-a-silver-bullet and falsification-not-exposure show matched-budget resampling ties or wins, and 260614530 notes repair after failure is rare. Highlighting by token probability gave no benefit (230207248) while edit-likelihood helped. Whether a per-requirement unit (test group) differs from line/edit localization, and whether confidence-guided repair vs regeneration is tested at matched budget, is unresolved; the v4_dprc scope decision also hinges on this.
suggested_searches: per-requirement test-group confidence code localization repair
confidence-guided targeted repair vs regeneration matched budget
self-written test adequacy model confidence correlation
